newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara says many banks within loan limits.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara says many banks within loan limits.

text.p: The Malaysian central bank said on Monday that many financial institutions were within the loan limits set by it for lending to the broad property sector and for buying shares.
In response to queries by national Bernama news agency, Bank Negara's deputy governor, Fong Weng Phak, said 26 commercial banks out of 37 in the country have not exceeded their lending limits.
"They include some of the very large commercial banks," he said.
In addition, Fong said 31 finance companies out of 40 had not reached the ceiling on property lending and all could still dish out loans for share purchases.
For merchant banks, two out of 12 could still lend out for property purchases and six could were below the ceiling for share purchases.
From April 1, the central bank imposed loan restrictions to the property sector and for buying shares, in a move to head off asset bubble.
Financial institutions were to limit their exposure to the property sector to 20 percent of total outstading loans. It also placed new restrictions on buying shares and stocks.
Fong said there are about 60 billion to 70 billion ringgit still available in the banking system to finance property and share purchases.
